mechanism_narrative: A sustained quarterly growth in real GDP (GDPC1) indicates robust economic expansion, which increases corporate earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: GDPC1 growth rate is positive in the most recent quarter but S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of such instances.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeds 0.5% for three consecutive months, it signals a monetary tightening cycle that increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where FEDFUNDS has been above 0.5% for three consecutive months, the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) and rise in payroll employment (PAYEMS) signals a strong labor market, which boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint decline in UNRATE and rise in PAYEMS occurs but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 60% of such instances over the 60-day horizon.

mechanism_narrative: During a late-cycle expansion regime, rising industrial production (INDPRO) indicates strong manufacturing activity and supply chain health, which supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In the late-cycle expansion regime, INDPRO growth is positive but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 60% of 20-day windows.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) fall below 600,000 units for two consecutive months, it signals a weakening housing market and reduced consumer confidence, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: HOUST falls below 600.0 for two consecutive months but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 60% of such cases.

mechanism_narrative: A rising consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) indicates increasing inflation, which typically leads to higher interest rates and reduced equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: CPIAUCSL growth rate is positive in the most recent month but S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in real personal consumption (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) signals strong consumer demand and confidence, which drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: RSAFS and HOUST both rise but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 60% of 5-day windows.

mechanism_narrative: In a high-unemployment regime (UNRATE > 8.0%), a decline in the unemployment rate signals a labor market recovery, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where UNRATE > 8.0%, a decline in UNRATE is observed but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 60% of 20-day windows.
